- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, creating a “peak-pullback” pattern.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show mean reversion or downward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often underestimates a falling trend until 2–3 days later.
- When true values show strong upward momentum (e.g., >87), model fails to capture the full extent of the rise, especially in the middle of the forecast.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp spikes and overestimates gradual declines.
- Model is prone to “overfitting” recent high values, leading to persistent overestimation when true values are trending down.
- Model often fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar-based patterns (e.g., end-of-month dips or holiday effects) — especially in the last 5–10 days.
- Model shows bias toward higher values in the first 10 days of forecast, then gradually adjusts — but often too late to catch downward momentum.
